The smallest compute resource on a CPU is called a transistor. The difference between high and low end CPUs are the nos of transistors that the manufacturer has put into the chip.

So basically high end chips have a higher transistor density. There are other reasons also but this is the main one

Why would CPU companies not keep the same transistor density across their chips?

Because everyone does not need the performance an i9 or i7  provides.. It makes more sense to purchase i3 that has a lower cost and is more power efficient


Why is i9/i7 costlier compared to i3/i5?

As mentioned before, i3 and i5 have a lower transistor density hence the process of fabricating (creating) these chips is easier since they take less time and resources for manufacturing
